title: Harcourt Trophies Grade 2 Teacher Guide — Alternative Teaching Strategies (Multi-Modal Skill Pages)
callouts: visual, kinesthetic and auditory models included in skill development
options are encouraged and HOMA can suggest which she feels will work best with the student

triModalTeachingStructure.description: Every Alternative Teaching Strategy page follows the EXACT same structure: Objective → Focus (direct instruction) → Reteach the Skill → Visual Model → Kinesthetic Model → Auditory Model → Summarize/Assess. Three different sensory pathways to the same skill. The parent picks whichever matches how their child learns best.

visual.description: Learning through seeing. Uses charts, written models, illustrations, diagrams, bulletin boards. Examples: write a knock-knock joke to teach questions vs. statements; write a story on chart paper and fill in a 'Setting Clues' chart; match sentence strips on a bulletin board.
examplesFromPages: T5: Write knock-knock joke on board — Person 2 asks questions, Person 1 makes statements. Children create a class joke book.
T7: Write 'Happy Town' story on chart paper, draw Setting Clues chart with Time and Place columns for children to fill in.
T8: Bulletin board with sentence strips — match naming parts (Jack and Jill, The Big Bad Wolf) with action parts (went up a hill, tricked Red Riding Hood).

kinesthetic.description: Learning through moving/doing. Uses physical cards, body movement, crafting, games. Examples: hold up punctuation cards when hearing statements vs. questions; play punctuation hopscotch on the sidewalk; build a shoebox diorama of a story setting; conduct a food survey.
examplesFromPages: T5: Children prepare period cards and question mark cards. Teacher reads sentences aloud — children hold up the matching card.
T6: Draw hopscotch squares on sidewalk with . ? ! in each square. Children hop, land on a punctuation mark, and say a sentence that matches it.
T7: Small groups build a shoebox diorama of the story setting using construction paper, modeling clay, and art supplies.
T8: Small groups conduct a 'Foods We Like' survey — poll classmates, write sentences about results, underline the naming parts.

auditory.description: Learning through hearing/speaking. Uses read-alouds, group discussion, acting out, listening exercises. Examples: act out an argument with a peacemaker asking questions; read sentences without punctuation and use voice to add correct inflection; listen to a passage and identify setting details.
examplesFromPages: T5: Groups of 3 — two children argue, third is peacemaker asking questions. Record questions and responses to share.
T6: Read items without inflection. Children decide how to read each properly. Add punctuation and re-read with correct voice.
T7: Teacher reads passage aloud, children identify time and place, describe details that reveal the setting.
T8: Read sentences aloud, children listen for and identify the naming part (who/what the sentence is about).

triModalTeachingStructure.value: Not all children learn the same way. Some need to see it, some need to touch/move it, some need to hear it. By offering all three, the parent always has an approach that works — and can try a different one if the first doesn't click.

reteachNotJustTeach.description: These pages are explicitly labeled 'Reteach the Skill' — they exist for when the main lesson didn't land. The tri-modal approach is the REMEDIATION strategy, not the first-pass instruction. This means the curriculum has a built-in recovery path.
reteachNotJustTeach.value: When a child doesn't get it the first time, the parent has three concrete next steps instead of repeating the same explanation louder.

summarizeAssessPattern.description: Every page ends with a Summarize/Assess section: have the child state what they learned in their own words, then apply it to stories they've already read. The assessment is oral and application-based, not another worksheet.
summarizeAssessPattern.value: The check for understanding is conversational, not test-like. Lower anxiety, higher signal.

playfulReteaching.description: The reteach activities are genuinely fun: make a class joke book, play punctuation hopscotch, build a diorama, conduct a food survey, act out an argument. These don't FEEL like reteaching — they feel like play. But the skill is embedded.
playfulReteaching.value: Children who need reteaching are often already frustrated. Fun activities reset the emotional state while still delivering the skill.

carolyngProductVision.quote: Love the visual, kinesthetic and auditory models included in skill development. Options are encouraged and HOMA can suggest which she feels will work best with the student
carolyngProductVision.interpretation: Carolyng is explicitly requesting that Homa act as a LEARNING STYLE ADVISOR — not just generating materials, but recommending WHICH teaching approach (visual, kinesthetic, auditory) will work best for a specific child. This is personalization at the teaching-strategy level, not just the content level. She wants Homa to know the child well enough to say 'try the kinesthetic version for this one.'
carolyngProductVision.implication: This requires a learner profile that tracks: which modalities have worked for this child, which skills they've struggled with, and what approach finally clicked. Over time, Homa could predict: 'For phonics, your child tends to do better with kinesthetic activities. Try the word-building manipulatives.'

overallLayout.structure: sectioned — top half is Objective + Focus + Reteach (Visual Model), bottom half is Kinesthetic + Auditory + Summarize/Assess
overallLayout.visualHierarchy: section headers in color (red for Reteach, blue for Kinesthetic/Auditory, green for Summarize), body text in black

difficulty.scaffolding: high — three different scaffolding approaches per skill

characters: nursery rhyme characters used in examples (Jack and Jill, Humpty Dumpty, Little Jack Horner, Old Mother Hubbard, Big Bad Wolf, Cinderella)
appealDrivers: playful reteach activities embedded in serious instruction

gaps.name: multi-modal-activity-set
gaps.description: For a given skill, generate THREE activity variants: visual (chart/diagram/written model), kinesthetic (physical game/craft/manipulative), and auditory (read-aloud/discussion/acting). Each targets the same learning objective through a different sensory pathway. Homa could recommend which to try based on the child's learner profile.

gaps.name: reteach-activity-bank
gaps.description: When a child doesn't demonstrate mastery on an assessment, generate fun reteach activities (hopscotch games, diorama projects, joke books, surveys) that embed the skill in play. Different from the original practice worksheet.

notes: Fifth drop from the Trophies system. This is the FIFTH layer: Alternative Teaching Strategies (remediation/reteaching with multi-modal approaches). Critically, Carolyng made a direct product suggestion: 'HOMA can suggest which she feels will work best with the student.' She's asking for learning-style-aware recommendations — Homa should know the child well enough to recommend visual vs. kinesthetic vs. auditory approaches. This is the first time she's described Homa as having agency/personality ('she feels') — she sees Homa as a teaching partner, not just a material generator.
